Actual αὕτη is a feminine this-one demonstrative. English this woman supplies its personal feminine designation without an independent Greek woman noun.

9:37.sourceText: ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ἀσθενήσασαν αὐτὴν ἀποθανεῖν· λούσαντες δὲ ἔθηκαν ἐν ὑπερῴῳ.
9:37.targetText: and it came to pass in those days she, having ailed, died, and having bathed her, they laid her in an upper chamber,

groups.note: Actual αὐτήν is the accusative personal subject of dying and the same woman immediately bathed and laid out. English states she, then her and her for those successive local roles; no new original pronouns are invented, and the actual accusative form remains.
Actual ἀποθανεῖν is an aorist dying infinitive under came-to-pass, rendered finite died. The original infinitive remains rather than an asserted Greek finite aorist.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with those days.

9:38.sourceText: ἐγγὺς δὲ οὔσης Λύδδας τῇ Ἰόππῃ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἀκούσαντες ὅτι Πέτρος ἐστὶν ἐν αὐτῇ ἀπέστειλαν δύο ἄνδρας πρὸς αὐτὸν παρακαλοῦντες Μὴ ὀκνήσῃς διελθεῖν ἕως ἡμῶν.
9:38.targetText: and Lydda being near to Joppa, the disciples having heard that Peter is in that [place], sent two men to him, calling on him not to delay to come through to them.

groups.note: Actual αὐτῇ is the dative feminine place-resuming pronoun referring to the named town. English that [place] makes that same place reference nominal; no independent Greek place noun is printed.
The actual sent-to personal recipient is also the immediately called-on person. English repeats him with calling on; both retain one written personal identity without a new original pronoun.

Actual ὀκνήσῃς is second-person aorist subjunctive under the negative direct request. LSV to delay follows the indirect infinitive report; the actual finite subject/mood remains, not a Greek infinitive at this word.

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 gives the direct request ἕως ἡμῶν, to us. LSV follows the TR indirect-request ἕως αὐτῶν, to them. The whole unlike written personal case construction remains explicit rather than substituting a third-person Greek pronoun for the actual first person.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV follows TR ἕως αὐτῶν to them in the indirect report. Pinned N1904 has the direct-request ἕως ἡμῶν to us; both the different written person and reporting frame remain explicit.

9:39.sourceText: ἀναστὰς δὲ Πέτρος συνῆλθεν αὐτοῖς· ὃν παραγενόμενον ἀνήγαγον εἰς τὸ ὑπερῷον, καὶ παρέστησαν αὐτῷ πᾶσαι αἱ χῆραι κλαίουσαι καὶ ἐπιδεικνύμεναι χιτῶνας καὶ ἱμάτια, ὅσα ἐποίει μετ’ αὐτῶν οὖσα ἡ Δορκάς.
9:39.targetText: And Peter having risen, went with them, whom having come, they brought into the upper chamber, and all the widows stood by him weeping, and showing coats and garments, as many as Dorcas was making while she was with them.

groups.note: Actual οὖσα is a present feminine being participle with Dorcas as its named subject. English while she was realizes that participial circumstance as a finite time clause without separately printed Greek while/she/was words.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with Dorcas.

9:40.sourceText: ἐκβαλὼν δὲ ἔξω πάντας ὁ Πέτρος καὶ θεὶς τὰ γόνατα προσηύξατο, καὶ ἐπιστρέψας πρὸς τὸ σῶμα εἶπεν Ταβειθά, ἀνάστηθι. ἡ δὲ ἤνοιξεν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῆς, καὶ ἰδοῦσα τὸν Πέτρον ἀνεκάθισεν.
9:40.targetText: And Peter having put them all forth outside, having bowed the knees, prayed, and having turned to the body, said, “Tabitha, arise”; and she opened her eyes, and having seen Peter, she sat up,

groups.note: Actual πάντας is substantival all-people as the putting-out object, rendered them all without an independently printed Greek them pronoun.
Actual θεὶς is the placing participle in the setting-the-knees idiom, rendered having bowed. Its source remains τίθημι rather than an independently printed bending verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with either Peter occurrence and her eyes.
Actual καί coordinates the putting-out and kneeling acts. English states the kneeling circumstance without separately rendering that conjunction.

9:41.sourceText: δοὺς δὲ αὐτῇ χεῖρα ἀνέστησεν αὐτήν· φωνήσας δὲ τοὺς ἁγίους καὶ τὰς χήρας παρέστησεν αὐτὴν ζῶσαν.
9:41.targetText: and having given her [his] hand, he lifted her up, and having called the holy ones and the widows, he presented her alive,

groups.note: The actual hand noun is the giving agent’s body part in the giving-a-hand action. English [his] hand makes that same understood bodily ownership explicit without a separately printed Greek possessive.

9:42.sourceText: γνωστὸν δὲ ἐγένετο καθ’ ὅλης τῆς Ἰόππης, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν πολλοὶ ἐπὶ τὸν Κύριον.
9:42.targetText: and it became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed on the LORD;

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with all Joppa.

9:43.sourceText: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἡμέρας ἱκανὰς μεῖναι ἐν Ἰόππῃ παρά τινι Σίμωνι βυρσεῖ.
9:43.targetText: and it came to pass, that he remained many days in Joppa, with a certain one, Simon a tanner.

groups.note: Actual μεῖναι is an aorist remaining infinitive under came-to-pass. English that he remained makes that event finite with its understood subject; no separate Greek that connector or he pronoun is printed.
